visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Logo]: 哈哈台 HahaTai. [Subtitle]: "Kiasu" is a Hokkien term 驚輸(kiasu) 源自福建話. (2) [Subtitle]: meaning "afraid to lose" 意思是「怕輸、怕吃虧」. (3) [Subtitle]: It became widely used in Singapore in the 1980s 1980年代開始在新加坡普及使用. (4) [Subtitle]: reflecting a competitive environment 表現出新加坡人重視競爭的社會氛圍. (5) [Subtitle]: One of my biggest culture shocks: 最大的一次文化震驚. (6) [Subtitle]: It's my mailbox in my house 是我在我家的信箱. (7) [Subtitle]: I saw a flyer in my mailbox 然後那個廣告單就是左講. (8) [Subtitle]: advertising coding and C language classes for two- to three-year-olds 給兩歲到三歲的小孩學Coding跟C language. (9) [Variety]: Coding 兩歲. (10) [Subtitle]: I don't even remember what I was doing at two 然後我想說我兩歲在幹嘛 我都不記得. (11) [Subtitle]: When I was two years old, I don't know if I can say 10 dollars 兩歲時我連媽媽十塊都不會講. (12) [Subtitle]: Interestingly, the word kiasu is very neutral and not a bad meaning 有趣的是 驚輸這個詞很中性 並不是貶意. (13) [Subtitle]: Do you feel offended if someone calls you "Kiasu"? 如果我講你們驚輸 你們會不開心嗎. narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: List-based: Term Definition -> Personal Anecdote -> Public Opinion -> Cultural Summary
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to explain the Singaporean cultural term 'Kiasu' (the fear of losing out) through a blend of educational narration and relatable street interviews. It explores how this competitive spirit manifests in daily life, such as extreme early-childhood education, while ultimately portraying the term as a neutral or even positive driver of the nation's success.
